name: SPENCER W. KIMBALL BUILDING
about: The university's administrative hub, where students find help with admissions, financial aid, registration, housing, and other campus services.
fact: A portrait of President Kimball unveiled at the building's dedication was painted by Ricks College alumnus Gregg Thorkelson.

source.title: BYU-Idaho Campus Tours - Spencer W. Kimball Building

name: JOHN TAYLOR BUILDING
about: A center for religious learning, with classrooms and a chapel used for lectures, worship, quiet study, and reflection.
fact: The chapel's custom organ combines real pipes with electronic voices: nine ranks of pipes work alongside 50 electronic voices.

source.title: BYU-Idaho Campus Tours - John Taylor Building

name: JACOB SPORI BUILDING - ORIGINAL
about: The historic heart of the early school, bringing classrooms and campus life together inside one building.
fact: In 1903, this single building accommodated the entire school! The much larger campus of today grew around this early landmark.

source.title: BYU-Idaho Campus Tours - Jacob Spori Building

name: JACOB SPORI BUILDING - REPLACEMENT
about: A home for visual art, design, and communication, including classrooms, creative workspaces, and the Spori Art Gallery.
fact: Pieces of the original building survive inside its replacement. Recovered woodwork, stone, and old bricks preserve traces of earlier students.

source.title: BYU-Idaho Campus Tours - Jacob Spori Building

name: OSCAR A. KIRKHAM BUILDING
about: A former campus gathering and performance building, remembered for its auditorium and the speakers who addressed students there.
fact: Former First Lady Eleanor Roosevelt spoke in the Kirkham Auditorium on March 2, 1959.

source.title: BYU-Idaho Campus Buildings - Kirkham Building

name: GEORGE S. ROMNEY BUILDING
about: A physical sciences building with teaching spaces for subjects such as chemistry, physics, and geology, plus a museum and planetarium.
fact: You can explore both the sky and the ground here: the building has an observatory and a seismology center that records distant earthquakes.

source.title: BYU-Idaho Campus Tours - George S. Romney Building

name: JOHN L. CLARKE BUILDING
about: A place to learn practical skills in nursing, home and family studies, early childhood education, cooking, and clothing design.
fact: Nursing students train in a simulated hospital, practicing patient care in realistic clinical settings before entering the workplace.

source.title: BYU-Idaho Campus Tours - John L. Clarke Building

name: JOHN W. HART BUILDING
about: A center for fitness, swimming, sports, and physical education, with gymnasiums, courts, classrooms, and a pool.
fact: Before the BYU-Idaho Center opened, the Hart also welcomed students for campus devotionals, firesides, and graduation ceremonies.

source.title: BYU-Idaho Campus Buildings - Hart Building

name: DAVID O. MCKAY LIBRARY
about: The university's library, supporting reading, research, quiet study, tutoring, and the preservation of campus history.
fact: In 2010, a skybridge connected the library's third floor to the Manwaring Center, linking two busy student destinations above ground level.

source.title: BYU-Idaho Campus Tours - David O. McKay Library

name: JOSEPH FIELDING SMITH BUILDING
about: An academic building where students develop skills in business, accounting, economics, languages, and communication.
fact: Students in the Integrated Business Core gain experience by running real companies, taking responsibility for marketing and daily operations.

source.title: BYU-Idaho Campus Tours - Joseph Fielding Smith Building

name: EZRA TAFT BENSON BUILDING
about: A life sciences building with laboratories, plant-growing facilities, and a wildlife museum that helps students explore the living world.
fact: Its jungle greenhouse offers a miniature green retreat, with lush plants, places to sit, and even a koi pond.

source.title: BYU-Idaho Campus Tours - Ezra Taft Benson Building

name: MARK AUSTIN BUILDING
about: A place for automotive learning, where students connect classroom knowledge with hands-on work on vehicles.
fact: Automotive students have held free vehicle-inspection nights, helping classmates check their cars while gaining practical experience.

source.title: BYU-Idaho Campus Buildings - Austin Building

name: HYRUM MANWARING STUDENT CENTER / MANWARING CENTER
about: A hub for student life, bringing together food, the University Store, activities, and places to meet friends between classes.
fact: After the Teton Dam failed in 1976, the Manwaring Center helped the community recover by providing meals and first aid.

source.title: BYU-Idaho Campus Tours - Hyrum Manwaring Center

name: ELIZA R. SNOW PERFORMING ARTS CENTER
about: A home for music and theatre, with rehearsal spaces, classrooms, theaters, and the Barrus Concert Hall.
fact: The Barrus Concert Hall's pipe organ contains 3,833 pipes. Its construction stretched across 21 years, from 1983 to 2004.

source.title: BYU-Idaho Campus Tours - Eliza R. Snow Building

name: HEATING PLANT
about: A utility building that supplied heat across campus.
fact: Steam traveled through insulated underground pipes to warm other campus buildings.

source.title: Steve Moser, History of Buildings at BYU-Idaho, pp. 22-23

name: WILLIAM F. RIGBY HALL
about: A campus building that has supported both student housing and the academic work of faculty members.
fact: Originally a men's dormitory, Rigby was later adapted into faculty office space, giving an old residence hall a new purpose.

source.title: BYU-Idaho Campus Buildings - Rigby Hall description

name: LOWELL G. BIDDULPH HALL
about: A former men's residence hall that later became space for university offices and services.
fact: Students originally knew this building as Ensign Hall. It received the name Lowell G. Biddulph Hall in 1995.

source.title: BYU-Idaho Campus Buildings - Biddulph Hall description

name: HELEN LAMPRECHT HALL
about: A residence hall that housed Ricks College students.
fact: Its student apartments became 37 family-housing units for winter semester 2002.

source.title: Steve Moser, History of Buildings at BYU-Idaho, p. 59

name: CHAPMAN HALL
about: A residence hall from the Ricks College years.
fact: Originally called Dorm 6, it received the name Chapman Hall on March 20, 1999.

source.title: Steve Moser, History of Buildings at BYU-Idaho, p. 59

name: PHYSICAL PLANT SHOP BUILDING
about: Maintenance workshops for university buildings and equipment.
fact: Its workshops included carpentry, painting, upholstery, and campus vehicle repairs.

source.title: Steve Moser, History of Buildings at BYU-Idaho, p. 50

name: GORDON B. HINCKLEY BUILDING
about: A teaching and gathering place for education and religion, with classrooms, chapels, and spaces for student activities.
fact: The building stands at the highest point on campus. Its entrance displays a portrait of the president who announced the move to BYU-Idaho.

source.title: BYU-Idaho Campus Tours - Gordon B. Hinckley Building

name: THOMAS E. RICKS BUILDING
about: A building for mathematics and the study of people and society, including subjects such as history, psychology, sociology, and political science.
fact: Faculty helped shape its design. Their input led to bright common areas with large windows where students could gather and study.

source.title: BYU-Idaho Campus Tours - Thomas E. Ricks Building

name: REXBURG IDAHO TEMPLE
about: A temple of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints beside the university, serving worshippers from Rexburg and the surrounding area.
fact: Most of its 700 art-glass windowpanes feature wheat stalks, designed by artist Tom Holdman.

source.title: Church Newsroom - Rexburg Idaho Temple Facts

name: BYU-IDAHO CENTER
about: The university's large gathering place for devotionals and major events, with additional space for recreation and student activities.
fact: Its auditorium seats 15,000 people, while its activity area is large enough to fit ten basketball courts.

source.title: BYU-Idaho Campus Buildings - BYU-Idaho Center

name: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY CENTER
about: A place where computing and engineering meet animal, food, and plant sciences through classrooms, laboratories, and practical projects.
fact: The building brings daylight inside through 1,096 exterior glass panels and 26 skylights.

source.title: BYU-Idaho Campus Tours - Science & Technology Building

name: VISUAL ARTS STUDIO
about: A hands-on art building with teaching spaces for ceramics and sculpture, plus facilities for working with clay, wood, and metal.
fact: Its glass-fronted lobby was designed as a student gallery, letting people outside see artwork as they walk past.

source.title: BYU-Idaho Newsroom - BYU-Idaho to Dedicate Three Buildings on Campus

name: ENGINEERING TECHNOLOGY CENTER
about: A practical learning center for automotive engineering, civil engineering, and construction management, with classrooms and specialized laboratories.
fact: This was once the Auxiliary Services Building, serving campus mail, printing, and supplies before being remodeled for engineering students.

source.title: BYU-Idaho Newsroom - BYU-Idaho to Dedicate Three Buildings on Campus
